title: RoadmapNode
description: Unit of work in a roadmap tree. Every file under roadmap/ at any depth validates against this schema, so a feature file and its parent share one format and can be subdivided the same way.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this schema the document targets. Bump the major when a removal or rename lands, the minor for additive fields.

id.description: Stable unique identifier across the whole roadmap. Never reused, never renumbered. Parent IDs live in the enclosing node's tasks[].

version.description: Version of this document's content. Bump the minor when fields change, the major when the scope changes.

name.description: Concise title. The root document uses "main".

description.description: What this node delivers and why, in a few sentences. Observable outcome, not an implementation list.

level.description: Depth of this node. A node with children is at most one level above them.

developmentType.description: Why this work exists. Defaults to ssd when omitted.

phase.description: SDD stage this node currently sits in. Optional on purpose: a node that spans stages, or whose stage is not yet decided, omits it rather than guessing. Expected on a leaf task that someone can pick up.

status.description: State of this node's work. A node is completed when every child is completed. blocked means it waits on something outside this roadmap; blockedBy lists internal dependencies.

openQuestions.description: Decisions needed before this node can reach ready. A node with open questions cannot be ready unless the user authorized it, which is recorded in decisions.

decisions.description: Authorizations the user granted that override a blocking question. Without an entry here, an open question is still open.

gitInfo.description: Branch bookkeeping. Omit when the project has no branch per node.

blockedBy.description: IDs of nodes in this roadmap that must complete first. Internal edges only; external reasons belong in openQuestions.

ref.description: Where the requirements, tests and documents that constrain this node live.

tests.description: Test IDs that verify this node.

design.description: A design document or an anchored section. A bare name that matches one of this node's own documents (specs.md, tests.md, traceability.md, design.md, verify.md) means that document of this node, and keeps resolving after archiving moves it. Anything else is a path relative to the project root, optionally with a #anchor, e.g. doc/es/F-01/design.md#order-status.

tasks.description: Children of this node. A child with its own file is a reference; a child inlined here is a leaf. JSON Schema cannot compare object members, so IDs must be unique and the dependency graph acyclic by construction: the agent checks both, and a validator or review catches regressions.

decision.description: A user authorization that resolved or overrode a blocking question.

question.description: The openQuestion text this decision answers, or the question the user chose to override.

resolution.description: What was decided, or that the user authorized proceeding with the risk unresolved.

authorizedBy.description: Who granted the authorization. Never an agent: the user authorizes, the agent records.

id.description: Unique within this node's children. MAIN- is reserved for the root.

description.description: The end-to-end behaviour this child makes work. Omit when the child is a bare reference.

phase.description: SDD stage this child is in. Omit when the child spans stages or the stage is undecided; expected on a leaf that someone can pick up.

decisions.description: User authorizations that released this child despite an open question.

file.description: Path to the child's document, relative to the directory holding this document. Siblings live together, so a child file is just <child-id>.json. Present when the child has its own document; omit for a leaf.

whatToBuild.description: One-sentence outcome statement. Prefer over description for leaves.

acceptanceCriteria.description: How a reviewer confirms this child is done. Vague criteria are worse than none.

then.description: A node that is ready or in apply must have every open question resolved, either removed or answered by a decision.
The root document is always MAIN-00 named main.
